cards.label: The next morning
cards.text: Archie texts an address in Shoreditch and the word "tonight". You arrive to find him outside a craft beer bar, looking mildly disgusted by its existence.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "Right. Same calc from the other night — I held onto it. Buyer's inside. Name's Marcus, finance, collects time-type for what he calls 'recreational use'. Don't ask. Just be normal. Or close to it."

cards.speaker: You
cards.text: "This is the same stuff. From when they tried to rob us."

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "Correct. Which is why having two of us is better than one. You're essentially a deterrent. Like a scarecrow. No offence."

Marcus is exactly what you expected: fleece, Patagonia, very clean trainers. He examines the calc with the careful enthusiasm of someone who has recently read about it online. He pays promptly, which is nice.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "See? Smooth as you like. Most of them are like Marcus. Professional, prompt, no Stanley knife. That's the market we're targeting."

cards.label: Walking back — Shoreditch High Street
cards.text: Archie splits the cash on the pavement outside a Pret. The city moves around you, completely indifferent to any of this.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "So. I've got a contact who knows a lot more about this than I do. Bloke called James — craftsman, Bermondsey. Takes raw calc and makes things out of it. Like the pearls. I've been meaning to introduce you."

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "I'll set it up. Give me a couple of days."
